solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Place to unburden dreadful lesson of Cain

definitions.note: a booth where sins are unloaded on a priest

indicators.note: dreadful says these three words are in a terrible state, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sermon on Cain's murder of Abel as a grim moral lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The booth in a church where penitents tell their sins to a priest is literally a place to unburden the conscience.

clue.text: Lion-headed monster to correspond with hawk-headed god

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree or correspond with it
Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown with a falcon's head

explanation.surface: A catalogue of mythical beasts with animal heads, Greek and Egyptian side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the fire-breathing beast had a lion's head, goat's body and serpent's tail.

clue.text: Nymphs in car heading north across main road

indicators.note: the car lies across the road, so its letters go round it
in a down clue, heading north means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a sedan is a saloon car
the A1, Britain's Great North Road, written AI; travelling north like the car in this down entry it reads upwards as IA

explanation.surface: Nymphs in a car driving up a trunk road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reads the car upwards, and the road, which runs the same way in a down entry, comes with it. 'across' sets the road inside. The A1 runs from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Naiads of Greek myth are water nymphs living in springs and rivers; this is the Latin-style plural.

clue.text: Comic, Eagle, keeping one enlightened

indicators.note: the eagle keeps the numeral inside it

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
I is the Roman numeral one
wise means knowing, enlightened

explanation.surface: A comic paper, the Eagle, keeps one reader enlightened.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eagle was a famous British boys' comic, so 'Comic, Eagle' reads as one title; in fact Comic is the definition. Ernie Wise was half of the comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was a British comedian, partner of Eric Morecambe, so he is an example of a comic.

clue.text: Spoken with vision, having been assigned position

indicators.note: spoken says the word for having vision is pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: someone sighted can see

explanation.surface: A seeing person, told where they are to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in a particular location has had its position allotted to it.

clue.text: Ring operator, ringing round, hinting at trouble

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped

indicators.note: the operator rings, surrounding the round letter

parts.note: minus is a mathematical operator
a round shape is O

explanation.surface: A telephone operator rings round, and the call hints at bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operator' suggests a switchboard, but it is the arithmetical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something menacing or foreboding hints at trouble to come.

clue.text: Answer four consecutive letters about an Asian currency

indicators.note: the four letters go about the word an

parts.note: F, G, H and I follow one another in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle answer made of a run of four letters about a currency of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four consecutive letters' does not say which four; the answer's crossing letters settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the monetary unit of Afghanistan, in Asia.

clue.text: Unexpansive, like John, Paul and George, but not Ringo

definitions.meaning: terse, speaking in curt short words

definitions.text: like John, Paul and George, but not Ringo
definitions.meaning: the first three Beatles' names have one syllable each, Ringo two

explanation.surface: A Beatle quiz: which trait did three share but not the drummer?
explanation.definitionFit: Words of one syllable make for curt, unexpansive speech, and John, Paul and George are one-syllable names.

clue.text: Potential cause of tears involving religious view

indicators.note: the vegetable involves, wraps round, the other piece

parts.note: chopping an onion makes the eyes water
pi is slang for pious, religious

explanation.surface: A religious view that might cause someone to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: A view held on a matter is one's belief or judgement about it.

clue.text: Temperature is uncontrollable: one coming in makes assessments

indicators.note: the numeral comes into the word for raging

parts.note: something that rages is out of control
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fever runs out of control as a patient arrives for assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is uncontrollable' looks like an anagram signal but gives RAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital staff who sort patients by urgency are judging, or assessing, each case.

clue.text: Make one joyous sound about another killing

indicators.note: the singing goes about the other sound

parts.note: to sing is to make a joyful sound
another joyous sound, laughter

explanation.surface: Someone happily making noises about a killing, in rather dark taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughtering is butchering, killing in large numbers.

clue.text: Unsettled duck in front of greenery when last rook departs

indicators.note: the duck's letter goes before the rest

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O

indicators.note: last says the later of the two Rs in the greenery word is the one that goes
departs says the letter for rook leaves the word

parts.note: verdure is green vegetation
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A duck on the lawn, the last rook flown off, still waiting to be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the second R leaves VERDUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill left unsettled past its date is late, still owing.

clue.text: Play including moon for miniature scene

indicators.note: the play includes the moon's name

parts.note: a drama is a play
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A stage play with a moon in it, presented as a model scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-dimensional model scene, as in a museum display case.

clue.text: Support given about engaging English poet

indicators.note: the reversed support engages, takes in, the letter for English
given about means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a stay is a prop or support

explanation.surface: Support offered to an English poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English poet' reads as one phrase, but English gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish Nobel-winning poet.

clue.text: Where midfielder may show skill casually

definitions.meaning: a football midfielder shows ability distributing the ball to teammates
said or mentioned incidentally, by the way

explanation.surface: A footballer showing off flair in an offhand way.
explanation.definitionFit: A midfielder shows skill in distributing the ball; a remark made by the way is offhand.

clue.text: Drunk bowled in to serve old Soviet executive

indicators.note: the drunk and bowled letters go in the serving word

parts.note: to pour drinks is to serve them
lit is slang for drunk
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A drunk dismissed in cricket, put to serve the old Soviet leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Soviet executive'; 'old' gives the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of the Soviet Communist Party.

clue.text: Zest shown by someone disappointing PM once

parts.note: a lemon is slang for a dud, a disappointing person or thing
Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister showing enthusiasm despite being a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the grated outer rind of citrus fruit, used in cooking.

clue.text: Again allow skinned fruit

parts.note: more means again, once more

indicators.note: skinned means the outer letters of the word are stripped off

explanation.surface: Permission, once more, to have peeled fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The morello is a sour dark cherry.

clue.text: Before dance catch game

indicators.note: before says the catching word goes ahead of the dance

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Catching something before a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport in which goals are scored through a high ring.

clue.text: Accessed butter, tonnes having been imported

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: something that butts, such as a goat
T is the abbreviation for tonnes

explanation.surface: Tonnes of butter imported and accessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts: a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: To have got at something is to have reached or obtained access to it.

clue.text: Sticky fare perhaps reasonable

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff
a dish is an example of food, or fare

explanation.surface: A sticky meal that is, perhaps, fairly decent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fairly good, though not excellent, is reasonable.

clue.text: Thanks for order in bar

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
pro means in favour of, for
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Thanking a server for taking an order in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for order' looks like a link and anagram signal, but each word gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is the bar of a pub or inn where beer is served from the tap.

clue.text: Attire worn by bishop?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the bishop's letter is set beside the rearranged attire

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: worn means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what a bishop wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' looks like plain clothing talk but rearranges ATTIRE with B.
explanation.definitionFit: This square cap is worn by Roman Catholic clergy, including bishops.

clue.text: Alpine ridge needs some spare tents

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mountaineer heading for a ridge needs extra tents.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'needs', which is a link word joining definition to wordplay; the ridge alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp mountain crest between glaciated valleys, the French word used in alpinism.

clue.text: Soldier shot back to cover second-in-command

indicators.note: the reversed word covers, surrounds, the chosen letter
back says the word is reversed

parts.note: a report is the bang of a gunshot

indicators.note: second-in picks the second letter of command

explanation.surface: A soldier shot in the back while protecting his deputy commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-in-command' reads as a deputy, but gives the second letter of 'command', O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalryman or private in a tank or armoured regiment is a trooper.

clue.text: Artwork featuring headless parrot inside wire bars

indicators.note: the trimmed parrot goes inside the cage

parts.note: a cage is made of wire bars

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Poll, Polly, is a traditional name for a parrot

explanation.surface: An artwork showing a decapitated parrot behind wires.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is a picture made by gluing scraps of paper and other materials to a backing.

clue.text: Nuncio upset about king's mythical creature

indicators.note: the jumbled envoy goes about the king's letter
upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R, for rex, is king; the 's is short for has

explanation.surface: A papal envoy upset about the king's legendary beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-horned horse of legend is a mythical beast.

clue.text: So he prefers a zip — sensible chap

definitions.meaning: read literally, his trousers have a zip, not a button fly
describes a shrewd, alert man not easily fooled

explanation.surface: A man's taste in trouser fastenings taken as proof of his good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone sharp and wise who cannot be fooled, so a shrewd fellow.
